name: coga/checkout-cleanup
description: The rules shared by everything that disposes of finished tickets and their feature checkouts — the checkout proofs retire and autoclose share, protecting primary checkouts and other clones, recovering from vanished `/tmp` checkouts, and `coga delete` — with terminal-owner cleanup and the branch-sweep archive in its leaves.
---

# Retiring tickets and checkouts

You do not delete your own feature branch. `coga retire` (manual, while the
ticket and its `## Dev` lines exist) and the daily autoclose sweep (for every
ticket it closes and every open `retires.md` entry) run one shared set of
[checkout proofs](#the-checkout-proofs). Ticket work no longer creates linked
worktrees ([coga/checkouts](../checkouts/SKILL.md)), so a current ticket
records only `branch:` and the disposal is branch-only. A ticket from the
retired linked-worktree layout may still record `worktree:`; the disposal
removes that worktree first, since a branch checked out in a linked worktree
cannot be deleted, then prunes the branch. Keep `worktree:` accurate where it
exists; it is what they act on.

This topic owns only what those jobs share. Each job's own procedure lives
with its ticket: `coga retire` in the packaged `bootstrap/retire/ticket.md`,
the autoclose and branch-sweep passes in the `recurring/autoclose-merged` and
`recurring/branch-sweep` templates. Implementation detail is in
[coga-dev/internals/branch-sweep](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/docs/contexts/coga-dev/internals/branch-sweep/SKILL.md).

## Leaves

- [coga/checkout-cleanup/terminal-owners](terminal-owners/SKILL.md) —
  terminal owners and closed PRs: ownership, durable branch debt,
  authorization, and when cleanup runs.
- [coga/checkout-cleanup/branch-sweep](branch-sweep/SKILL.md) — branch-sweep
  protection, the `retired/<branch>` archive, and
  `[git] worktrees_ticket_owned`.

## The checkout proofs

A recorded worktree is removed only when:

- Git identifies it as a linked worktree of the same repository, still on the
  recorded branch;
- no other non-terminal ticket in any Coga workspace of the same Git checkout
  records that branch or worktree (a refused or incomplete claim scan keeps
  even a branch-only disposal pending, which autoclose reports and retains);
- no PR for that head is open;
- the branch has landed on control or still equals the recorded merged PR head.

After these proofs, every branch the ticket owns (each `## Dev` `branch:`
line) that is still present locally or on the remote goes through the branch
sweep restricted to those names, under the
[terminal-owner rule](terminal-owners/SKILL.md) and the
[archive gate](branch-sweep/SKILL.md). Each candidate gets its own
cross-workspace live-claim check first. A kept branch is reported with its
reason, and the disposal stays pending while its local ref survives. This
step is skipped while the recorded worktree survives.

Local cleanup precedes remote deletion. Local deletion deletes only the tip
it authorized; remote deletion re-verifies the exact head and uses
force-with-lease, so a reused branch is never deleted on stale PR state. A
forced local delete logs the deleted tip SHA for reflog recovery.

**Ignored state.** Tracked, untracked, and ignored files all preserve the
checkout, except regenerable caches (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`,
`.ruff_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, and Coga's rebuilt `.agent-skills/` symlink
view), which retire deletes and counts. A copied `coga.local.toml` is judged
by content: byte-identical to the operator's own (`COGA_LOCAL_CONFIG` when
set) it is deleted and counted, since the original survives; an edited copy
preserves the checkout. Other machine-local state (`.env`, `.venv/`,
`.coga/`, agent discovery links) preserves it. For ignored-only state retire
prints and records the explicit opt-in `git worktree remove --force
'<path>'`; it never offers that over tracked or untracked work.

Reported for manual disposal: a stale linked worktree now on another branch;
a checkout shared with another live ticket or an open PR; a locked or dirty
worktree; and a recorded path already gone (reported, not pruned).

## Primary checkouts and other clones

A primary checkout is never directory debt, including another clone's primary
and independent sandbox clones: Git topology cannot prove a clone disposable,
and it may hold untracked or ignored data. Autoclose preserves such a
directory and never recommends deleting it.

The branch stays debt in the repository that owns it, recorded as the entry's
`owner` for foreign primary and foreign linked checkouts. A foreign
checkout's branch is never judged in the invoking clone, under autoclose or
`coga retire`: a same-named branch there is left untouched. While the
recorded worktree exists and is not this repository's linked worktree or
primary (a foreign linked worktree, another repository's primary, or a
directory Git cannot classify), `checkout_disposal.dispose_checkout` skips
all branch cleanup in the invoking clone with one note saying why, and leaves
the directory in place. If inspecting the path or its ownership raises an
error, cleanup records the failure and preserves the branch. Once a primary
checkout's directory is gone, autoclose judges its branch only through the
recorded `owner`. Foreign
worktrees are expected only for recurring; elsewhere such a record is a
stray. A remaining foreign branch is reported for manual cleanup in its
owning clone. The owning clone's own daily branch sweep runs the ordinary
proofs on the entries that record it as `owner`, then discharges and
publishes them (`coga/recurring/scheduling`), so the manual step remains only
for a clone that does not run `coga recurring`. An unreadable owner or branch
list keeps the entry pending, and so does a missing owner of a foreign linked
worktree. Once the owner's branch is gone, a primary-checkout entry
discharges with no directory deletion or manual `retires.md` edit; foreign
linked worktrees still owe their directory cleanup.

### Accepted disappearance policy

For an independent clone recorded as its own owner, a missing directory is
treated as deletion of the clone and its branch, so the entry clears. A
missing path does not prove deletion — relocation or a temporarily
unavailable filesystem looks the same — but automatic discharge keeps deleted
sandbox clones from generating reminders forever. The cost: a surviving
clone's branch cleanup can be forgotten if its recorded path disappears. The
policy drops bookkeeping only; it never deletes a clone.

Before moving or renaming a clone, pause autoclose sweeps in every
participating checkout, update both `owner` and `worktree` in its
`retires.md` entries to the new path (using the worklist's field encoding),
and update any surviving ticket's `worktree:`. Move the clone and verify the
new path before resuming sweeps. For a temporary unmount, keep sweeps paused
until the original path is back. Publish ephemeral work before deliberately
removing a clone; that removal also discharges its entry.

## `/tmp` checkouts do not survive; the branch does

Treat any checkout under the system temp dir (a sandbox clone, a Dream or
Retro run checkout, an ad-hoc review worktree) as ephemeral: it is routinely
gone by the time anyone acts on it. Leaving work "preserved" in one, or
recording its path in `worktree:` or a blackboard note, preserves nothing.
Before the run ends, push the branch or land its commits on `main`.

When a linked `/tmp` worktree vanishes, Git keeps two things: a stale
registration (`git worktree prune` clears it; the branch sweep runs it) and
the local branch, which may now be the only copy of unlanded commits. A stale
`worktree:` line pointing at a gone path is therefore not evidence the work
landed. Recover from the primary checkout after refreshing `main` from `origin`
(here, as in `coga/checkouts`, `origin` and `main` stand for the configured
`[git].remote` and `[git].control_branch`):

1. Inspect `git log main..<branch>` for candidate commits. Squash merges and
   cherry-picks may already have landed their changes; check merged-PR
   history or patch equivalence before selecting commits to recover.
2. Recover only work still missing and wanted: cherry-pick onto `main` through
   the normal publication path, or `git push origin <branch>` and open a PR.
3. Only then `git branch -D <branch>`.

## `coga delete <slug>`

Removes a task directory (ticket, blackboard, attachments) and syncs the
removal; recovery is `git restore`, with no Slack broadcast. Use it for an
abandoned ticket with nothing to retro. `coga run delete-task <slug>` does
the same removal without syncing. Both hold the checkout-local state lock.
Bootstrap tickets are not deletable. `--keep-control-checkout` is the
Retro-only form: accepted only from a linked worktree, it still pushes to the
remote control branch but does not fast-forward another checkout that has
control checked out; from the primary checkout it fails before deleting. In a
sandbox that cannot create a linked worktree, Retro may use an independent
clone and plain `coga delete`.

title: Retire a finished ticket
---

## Description

Command ticket for the `retire` verb, and the owner of its contract. It has no
agent phase: launch runs the sibling `ticket.py` with the verb's argv
([coga/script-tickets](context:coga/script-tickets)), and this file describes
what that script does. It creates no task for itself and writes no
blackboard.

`coga retire <slug> [--agent <type>] [--no-launch]` is a default alias for
`coga launch bootstrap/retire -- <slug> ...`. The `--` keeps `--agent` and
`--no-launch` away from launch's own options so they reach the script.
`coga retire --help` prints the script's usage; like any launch, it needs a
configured workspace (`coga.local.toml` with a user).

### Why done and canceled differ

Owner decision, 2026-10-13: positive learning already landed in the merged PR
(the same PR updates the owning topic), and negative learning lives in the
ticket, usually as the cancellation reason. So a **done** ticket is retired
deterministically, with no agent, and a **canceled** ticket gets a Retro task
that extracts the cancellation reason and any other negative learning before
deleting it.

### Steps

1. **Refuse unless finished.** The slug resolves like any task ref (unique
   prefix included). An unknown slug, a status other than `done` or
   `canceled`, or a configuration error exits 2.
2. **Dispose of the checkout.** Read `branch:`, `worktree:` and `pr:` from
   the ticket's `## Dev` section while the ticket still exists, and dispose of
   the recorded worktree and every owned branch under the
   [checkout proofs](context:coga/checkout-cleanup), including the
   [terminal-owner rule](context:coga/checkout-cleanup/terminal-owners).
   Primary checkouts and other clones are never disposed of
   ([coga/checkout-cleanup](context:coga/checkout-cleanup)). This runs only from
   a checkout on `[git].control_branch`: off control, with `[git].enabled`
   false, or outside a Git work tree, retire prints
   `Retire: checkout cleanup skipped ...` and leaves the checkout and branch to
   autoclose or `branch-sweep`.
3. **A kept checkout is a bug.** The ticket is the checkout's only owner
   record, so a worktree or owned branch the proofs kept must not lose it.
   Retire skips the worklist discharge and exits 2:
   - done: it deletes and creates nothing; fix the checkout by hand and run
     `coga retire` again.
   - canceled: it creates the retire task already `blocked` with what it kept
     and why (which notifies the owner, as `coga block` does) and launches
     nothing; fix the checkout, then `coga unblock` and `coga launch` the
     retire task.
4. **Discharge the worklist.** Drop the slug from any recurring template's
   `retires.md`, but only once its local branch is gone (judged in the owning
   repository when the entry records another clone as `owner`) and its
   recorded worktree directory is gone or is a repository's primary checkout.
   A worklist error is reported, never fatal.
5. **Done: delete.** Remove the task as `coga delete` does and publish the
   removal (`Ticket: <slug> — deleted (retire)`); recover with `git restore`.
6. **Canceled: Retro.** Scaffold `retire-<slug>` straight to `active` on the
   one-step `direct/body` workflow, its body rendered from the `retire.md`
   resource (a repo override substitutes only `{slug}`), and publish it
   (`Ticket: retire-<slug> — created (retire)`). The body invokes the
   `retro/done-ticket` skill, which opens the PR that records `## Retro`,
   edits knowledge if warranted, and deletes the source task in the same PR.
   `--agent` picks that task's main agent (default: the configured default
   agent); a canceled retire with no agent configured exits 2. Retire then
   launches the task in-process and exits with its code, unless
   `--no-launch`, which prints the `coga launch` command instead. If that
   launch kept local changes after a refused checkout return, retire exits 75
   so the outer launch neither refreshes the checkout nor sweeps them.

`--agent` and `--no-launch` affect only step 6. Branches with no live ticket
are the `branch-sweep` job's.

Deleting a source task breaks every durable reference that resolves it

name: coga/checkout-cleanup
description: The rules shared by everything that disposes of finished tickets and their feature checkouts — the checkout proofs retire and autoclose share, protecting primary checkouts and other clones, recovering from vanished `/tmp` checkouts, and `coga delete` — with terminal-owner cleanup and the branch-sweep archive in its leaves.

# Retiring tickets and checkouts

You do not delete your own feature branch. `coga retire` (manual, while the
ticket and its `## Dev` lines exist) and the daily autoclose sweep (for every
ticket it closes and every open `retires.md` entry) run one shared set of
[checkout proofs](#the-checkout-proofs). Ticket work no longer creates linked
worktrees ([coga/checkouts](../checkouts/SKILL.md)), so a current ticket
records only `branch:` and the disposal is branch-only. A ticket from the
retired linked-worktree layout may still record `worktree:`; the disposal
removes that worktree first, since a branch checked out in a linked worktree
cannot be deleted, then prunes the branch. Keep `worktree:` accurate where it
exists; it is what they act on.

This topic owns only what those jobs share. Each job's own procedure lives
with its ticket: `coga retire` in the packaged `bootstrap/retire/ticket.md`,
the autoclose and branch-sweep passes in the `recurring/autoclose-merged` and
`recurring/branch-sweep` templates. Implementation detail is in
[coga-dev/internals/branch-sweep](https://github.com/FastJVM/coga/blob/main/docs/contexts/coga-dev/internals/branch-sweep/SKILL.md).

## Leaves

- [coga/checkout-cleanup/terminal-owners](terminal-owners/SKILL.md) —
  terminal owners and closed PRs: ownership, durable branch debt,
  authorization, and when cleanup runs.
- [coga/checkout-cleanup/branch-sweep](branch-sweep/SKILL.md) — branch-sweep
  protection, the `retired/<branch>` archive, and
  `[git] worktrees_ticket_owned`.

## The checkout proofs

A recorded worktree is removed only when:

- Git identifies it as a linked worktree of the same repository, still on the
  recorded branch;
- no other non-terminal ticket in any Coga workspace of the same Git checkout
  records that branch or worktree (a refused or incomplete claim scan keeps
  even a branch-only disposal pending, which autoclose reports and retains);
- no PR for that head is open;
- the branch has landed on control or still equals the recorded merged PR head.

After these proofs, every branch the ticket owns (each `## Dev` `branch:`
line) that is still present locally or on the remote goes through the branch
sweep restricted to those names, under the
[terminal-owner rule](terminal-owners/SKILL.md) and the
[archive gate](branch-sweep/SKILL.md). Each candidate gets its own
cross-workspace live-claim check first. A kept branch is reported with its
reason, and the disposal stays pending while its local ref survives. This
step is skipped while the recorded worktree survives.

Local cleanup precedes remote deletion. Local deletion deletes only the tip
it authorized; remote deletion re-verifies the exact head and uses
force-with-lease, so a reused branch is never deleted on stale PR state. A
forced local delete logs the deleted tip SHA for reflog recovery.

**Ignored state.** Tracked, untracked, and ignored files all preserve the
checkout, except regenerable caches (`__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`,
`.ruff_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, and Coga's rebuilt `.agent-skills/` symlink
view), which retire deletes and counts. A copied `coga.local.toml` is judged
by content: byte-identical to the operator's own (`COGA_LOCAL_CONFIG` when
set) it is deleted and counted, since the original survives; an edited copy
preserves the checkout. Other machine-local state (`.env`, `.venv/`,
`.coga/`, agent discovery links) preserves it. For ignored-only state retire
prints and records the explicit opt-in `git worktree remove --force
'<path>'`; it never offers that over tracked or untracked work.

Reported for manual disposal: a stale linked worktree now on another branch;
a checkout shared with another live ticket or an open PR; a locked or dirty
worktree; and a recorded path already gone (reported, not pruned).

## Primary checkouts and other clones

A primary checkout is never directory debt, including another clone's primary
and independent sandbox clones: Git topology cannot prove a clone disposable,
and it may hold untracked or ignored data. Autoclose preserves such a
directory and never recommends deleting it.

The branch stays debt in the repository that owns it, recorded as the entry's
`owner` for foreign primary and foreign linked checkouts. A foreign
checkout's branch is never judged in the invoking clone, under autoclose or
`coga retire`: a same-named branch there is left untouched. While the
recorded worktree exists and is not this repository's linked worktree or
primary (a foreign linked worktree, another repository's primary, or a
directory Git cannot classify), `checkout_disposal.dispose_checkout` skips
all branch cleanup in the invoking clone with one note saying why, and leaves
the directory in place. If inspecting the path or its ownership raises an
error, cleanup records the failure and preserves the branch. Once a primary
checkout's directory is gone, autoclose judges its branch only through the
recorded `owner`. Foreign
worktrees are expected only for recurring; elsewhere such a record is a
stray. A remaining foreign branch is reported for manual cleanup in its
owning clone. The owning clone's own daily branch sweep runs the ordinary
proofs on the entries that record it as `owner`, then discharges and
publishes them (`coga/recurring/scheduling`), so the manual step remains only
for a clone that does not run `coga recurring`. An unreadable owner or branch
list keeps the entry pending, and so does a missing owner of a foreign linked
worktree. Once the owner's branch is gone, a primary-checkout entry
discharges with no directory deletion or manual `retires.md` edit; foreign
linked worktrees still owe their directory cleanup.

### Accepted disappearance policy

For an independent clone recorded as its own owner, a missing directory is
treated as deletion of the clone and its branch, so the entry clears. A
missing path does not prove deletion — relocation or a temporarily
unavailable filesystem looks the same — but automatic discharge keeps deleted
sandbox clones from generating reminders forever. The cost: a surviving
clone's branch cleanup can be forgotten if its recorded path disappears. The
policy drops bookkeeping only; it never deletes a clone.

Before moving or renaming a clone, pause autoclose sweeps in every
participating checkout, update both `owner` and `worktree` in its
`retires.md` entries to the new path (using the worklist's field encoding),
and update any surviving ticket's `worktree:`. Move the clone and verify the
new path before resuming sweeps. For a temporary unmount, keep sweeps paused
until the original path is back. Publish ephemeral work before deliberately
removing a clone; that removal also discharges its entry.

## `/tmp` checkouts do not survive; the branch does

Treat any checkout under the system temp dir (a sandbox clone, a Dream or
Retro run checkout, an ad-hoc review worktree) as ephemeral: it is routinely
gone by the time anyone acts on it. Leaving work "preserved" in one, or
recording its path in `worktree:` or a blackboard note, preserves nothing.
Before the run ends, push the branch or land its commits on `main`.

When a linked `/tmp` worktree vanishes, Git keeps two things: a stale
registration (`git worktree prune` clears it; the branch sweep runs it) and
the local branch, which may now be the only copy of unlanded commits. A stale
`worktree:` line pointing at a gone path is therefore not evidence the work
landed. Recover from the primary checkout after refreshing `main` from `origin`
(here, as in `coga/checkouts`, `origin` and `main` stand for the configured
`[git].remote` and `[git].control_branch`):

1. Inspect `git log main..<branch>` for candidate commits. Squash merges and
   cherry-picks may already have landed their changes; check merged-PR
   history or patch equivalence before selecting commits to recover.
2. Recover only work still missing and wanted: cherry-pick onto `main` through
   the normal publication path, or `git push origin <branch>` and open a PR.
3. Only then `git branch -D <branch>`.

## `coga delete <slug>`

Removes a task directory (ticket, blackboard, attachments) and syncs the
removal; recovery is `git restore`, with no Slack broadcast. Use it for an
abandoned ticket with nothing to retro. `coga run delete-task <slug>` does
the same removal without syncing. Both hold the checkout-local state lock.
Bootstrap tickets are not deletable. `--keep-control-checkout` is the
Retro-only form: accepted only from a linked worktree, it still pushes to the
remote control branch but does not fast-forward another checkout that has
control checked out; from the primary checkout it fails before deleting. In a
sandbox that cannot create a linked worktree, Retro may use an independent
clone and plain `coga delete`.

    """Delete a done task and sync the removal, with no retro agent.

    A kept checkout refuses before anything is deleted: the ticket is that
    checkout's only owner record, so it stays on disk with its `## Dev` lines
    and retire exits 2. Nothing else is created; the owner fixes the checkout
    by hand and runs `coga retire` again.
    """
    if refusal is not None:
        _bail(
            f"Retire refused: {refusal} {ref.id_slug} was not deleted; fix the "
            f"checkout, then run `coga retire {ref.id_slug}` again."
        )
    try:
        output = run_delete_task(cfg, ref)
    except DeleteTaskError as exc:
        _bail(str(exc))
    typer.echo(f"Retire: {output}", nl=False)
    try:
        git.publish(
            cfg,
            [ref.path, log_path(cfg)],
            f"Ticket: {ref.id_slug} — deleted (retire)",
        )
    except GitError as exc:
        typer.secho(f"[git] sync failed: {exc}", fg=typer.colors.YELLOW, err=True)

---
name: bootstrap/delete-task
description: Remove a task directory from the working tree — the contract behind `coga delete` and the `delete-task` registered recipe.
---

# Delete Task

Remove a Coga task — its `ticket.md` (and, in directory form, the task
directory and any siblings) — from the working tree. Recovery is via `git restore`; git
history is the audit trail, so deletion posts no Slack broadcast.

There is one implementation of task deletion, `coga.delete_task`, reached by
two spellings. `coga delete <task>` resolves the task, removes it, and syncs
the removal to the control branch. `coga run delete-task <task>` is the bare
working-tree removal with no sync — the spelling to use from inside another
task's session, where the caller owns when the deletion lands.

Both spellings hold the checkout-local spawn-admission barrier around the
filesystem removal. A megalaunch child that is still held after its final proof
therefore cannot be released for a task that this recipe deleted in the gap.

Deletion keys off the resolved ticket path: a `<dir>/ticket.md` means a
directory-form task, so it removes that one task directory; a `tasks/<slug>.md`
means a file-form task, so it removes that single file only and never touches
the shared parent. It refuses a target that is not a file, so it can never be
pointed at an arbitrary directory.

## Known Skill Contract

- Purpose: remove a single task (file or directory) from the working tree.
- Runs: `coga run delete-task <task>`, or `coga delete <task>` when the
  removal should also land on the control branch.
- Inputs: the task ref, resolved the same way every other Coga command
  resolves one. The ticket path's name discriminates the form (`ticket.md` →
  directory form; `<slug>.md` → file form).
- May change: under the spawn-admission barrier, deletes exactly the one named
  task — its directory (directory form) or its single `.md` file (file form).
  No other file, ref, or lifecycle state, and never a shared parent directory.
- Action: `direct-fix`
- Idempotency: existence is checked before the single delete; there is no
  partial state to reconcile. The caller (`coga delete`, or a Dream worker) is
  responsible for not dispatching a target twice.
- Stop and ask: the task ref does not resolve, or the resolved ticket is not a
  file — the recipe exits non-zero without deleting anything.
- Output: prints `<slug>: deleted <path>` to stdout. No Slack broadcast, no
  blackboard write.
1. **Refuse unless finished.** The slug resolves like any task ref (unique
   prefix included). An unknown slug, a status other than `done` or
   `canceled`, or a configuration error exits 2.
2. **Dispose of the checkout.** Read `branch:`, `worktree:` and `pr:` from

description: Remove a task directory from the working tree — the contract behind `coga delete` and the `delete-task` registered recipe.

# Delete Task

Remove a Coga task — its `ticket.md` (and, in directory form, the task
directory and any siblings) — from the working tree. Recovery is via `git restore`; git
history is the audit trail, so deletion posts no Slack broadcast.

There is one implementation of task deletion, `coga.delete_task`, reached by
two spellings. `coga delete <task>` resolves the task, removes it, and syncs
the removal to the control branch. `coga run delete-task <task>` is the bare
working-tree removal with no sync — the spelling to use from inside another
task's session, where the caller owns when the deletion lands.

filesystem removal. A megalaunch child that is still held after its final proof
therefore cannot be released for a task that this recipe deleted in the gap.

means a file-form task, so it removes that single file only and never touches
the shared parent. It refuses a target that is not a file, so it can never be
pointed at an arbitrary directory.

- Purpose: remove a single task (file or directory) from the working tree.

  task — its directory (directory form) or its single `.md` file (file form).

  partial state to reconcile. The caller (`coga delete`, or a Dream worker) is
  responsible for not dispatching a target twice.

  file — the recipe exits non-zero without deleting anything.

  blackboard write.

spec='''## Description

Deleting a ticket can leave README, topic, skill, or code references pointing
at a path that no longer exists on the control branch. Retro already searches
for and reviews those references, but ordinary `coga delete`, the `delete-task`
recipe, and deterministic retirement of done tickets bypass that procedure.
Add a visible advisory diagnostic to their shared deletion path. Preserve
unattended deletion and existing exit/publication contracts; this is a warning,
not a proof that a link is broken or a refusal gate.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Before filesystem removal, `coga delete`, `coga run delete-task`, and
  done-ticket `coga retire` report candidate inbound references on stderr.
  Each diagnostic identifies the deleted task and referring repo-relative
  file and line, says deletion will continue, and advises inspecting live
  references and pinning them to a commit containing the ticket before
  deleting (or restoring the ticket and repairing afterward).
- [ ] Search tracked working-tree files with literal matching for both the
  resolved task's Git-root-relative removal path and its final slug component
  without `.md`. This catches control-branch URLs, full paths, and relative
  file/directory links, including nested task slugs. Resolve paths from config
  and `TaskRef`, never by assuming `coga/tasks` or the invocation directory.
- [ ] Exclude the configured tasks root (all transient tickets), configured
  global log file, and `docs/archive/**` before reading file contents. Scan
  from the actual Git root, including files outside a nested Coga workspace.
  Do not read untracked/ignored files or follow symlinks out of the tree.
  Duplicate pattern matches on one source line produce one diagnostic entry.
- [ ] Describe hits as *possible references*: longer slugs, fixture text, and
  existing commit permalinks can match and require human inspection. No
  Markdown parser or semantic link classifier is required. No claim that a
  quiet search proves deletion safe; untracked content, excluded trees, and
  other checkouts are outside this check.
- [ ] A successful scan with no matches is quiet. Disabled Git, missing Git,
  a non-Git workspace, or a failed scan produces one concise stderr warning
  that references were not checked, and deletion still proceeds. A grep exit
  of 1 means no matches; other failures must not masquerade as a clean scan.
  Expected scan failures never escape as tracebacks or `DeleteTaskError`.
- [ ] Existing stdout deletion reports, success/error exit codes, task-shape
  safety, checkout lock, publication boundaries, and retire checkout refusal
  stay intact. No confirmation, force flag, Slack notification, link edit,
  new task, or Retro agent is added for done-ticket retirement.
- [ ] Recurring same-path replacement does not warn about links to the path it
  immediately recreates. Ordinary removal, including recurring promotion,
  uses the shared warning behavior. Cover this exception explicitly rather
  than relying on a caller discarding the deletion report.
- [ ] Regression tests cover all three command routes, both ticket shapes,
  nested/custom workspace paths, working-tree edits to tracked references,
  exclusions, false positives, no matches, scan errors/unavailable Git, and
  the recurring replacement exception. Verify warning emission occurs while
  the target still exists and that deletion/publication outcomes remain the
  existing ones.
- [ ] Update the owning shared deletion topic and dependent shipped surfaces
  in the implementation PR; keep Retro's stronger search-and-repair duty.
  Record Linux checks under `coga-dev/testing`; native checks defer to release.

### Proposed shape

1. Extend `src/coga/delete_task.py`, `run_delete_task()`, with a small private
   advisory scan invoked after validating the target and before unlink/rmtree
   under the existing `git.state_lock`. Keep the returned stdout report
   unchanged; emit diagnostics to stderr so callers that ignore the return
   value cannot silently discard warnings. Use argument-vector subprocesses,
   literal Git pathspecs, and stable non-color output; distinguish grep's
   no-match status from failure. Discover the Git root through existing Git
   infrastructure and construct the two literal search patterns from the
   resolved target. Exclude restricted paths in the command, not by filtering
   already-read matches. Do not dynamically parse agent instructions.
2. Add a narrowly named keyword-only suppression for same-path replacement
   (for example `warn_inbound=True`), and opt out only at the replacement
   call in `src/coga/recurring.py`, `materialize_period()`. Verify the actual
   enclosing symbol while implementing. Leave promotion on the default.
   Do not add a CLI opt-out or a configuration setting.
3. Keep `src/coga/commands/delete.py`, `delete()`, and the recipe adapter
   `run_delete_task_recipe()` thin. The packaged retire script's
   `_delete_done_task()` already calls the same function; it inherits the
   diagnostic and retains its deterministic deletion/publication procedure.
   Retire will not repoint links: literal matches cannot safely determine
   intent, and doc edits need a reviewable change alongside deletion. An
   operator who needs prevention must inspect and repair before invocation;
   this advisory command cannot pause for that work.
4. The scan belongs with shared task deletion: `delete()`,
   `run_delete_task_recipe()`, and retire's `_delete_done_task()` consume that
   exact shared symbol, with recurring removal as another consumer. This
   meets the microkernel shared-infrastructure rule, and the registered
   `delete-task` recipe already has a co-versioned argv/report/exit contract.
   Do not introduce a new command, recipe, plugin, or general link checker.
5. Put the shared advisory contract in the packaged
   `coga/checkout-cleanup` topic's `coga delete` section. Summarize and link it
   from `bootstrap/delete-task` and `bootstrap/retire`; adjust the retire
   resource, lifecycle/knowledge summaries, and Retro text only where their
   descriptions would otherwise contradict the new warning. The stronger
   Retro procedure still owns classification and permalink repair, while
   core reports candidates only. Add regressions primarily in
   `tests/test_commands.py` and `tests/test_retire.py`, with recurring and
   package-template assertions where affected.

### Out of scope

Automatic reference repair; refusal on matches; changing done-versus-canceled
retirement; changing Retro's PR procedure; checking external repos, remote
pages, or untracked files; parsing arbitrary repo search policies; introducing
configuration for scan exclusions; exhaustive URL/Markdown validation; changing
publication semantics or the generic state sweep.

## Context

- `src/coga/delete_task.py`, `run_delete_task()`, holds `git.state_lock`,
  validates `TaskRef.ticket_path`, and chooses `rmtree` for `ticket.md` versus
  `unlink` for file-form tickets. `run_delete_task_recipe()` resolves one
  argument and prints that function's report without publishing.
- `src/coga/commands/delete.py`, `delete()`, calls `run_delete_task()` then
  publishes only the resolved task path and `paths.log_path(cfg)` through
  `git.publish()`. Therefore reference edits cannot be assumed to land
  atomically with a human delete.
- `src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/retire/ticket.py`,
  `retire()`, routes done tickets to `_delete_done_task()` after cleanup;
  `_delete_done_task()` calls `run_delete_task()` then `git.publish()`.
  The contract owner is its sibling `ticket.md`; `src/coga/resources/retire.md`
  is the generated canceled-ticket agent task body, not the deterministic
  done-ticket implementation.
- `src/coga/recurring.py` calls `run_delete_task()` both during serviced period
  replacement and promotion; distinguish recreation from permanent removal
  when adding the diagnostic. `src/coga/tasks.py`, `TaskRef.ticket_path` and
  `TaskRef.id_slug`, supply resolved identity rather than the user's prefix.
- Cited rather than attached: read `coga-dev/microkernel` at
  `docs/contexts/coga-dev/microkernel/SKILL.md`, “The microkernel rule” and
  “The kernel tier and its edges”, for the shared-symbol and recipe boundary.
- Cited rather than attached: read `coga/checkout-cleanup` at
  `src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/contexts/coga/checkout-cleanup/SKILL.md`,
  “coga delete”, for the owning deletion contract, and `coga/knowledge` at
  the sibling `knowledge/SKILL.md`, “Where knowledge lives” and “Narrative
  links, never restates”, for ownership and dependent-surface updates.
- Read the packaged `retro/done-ticket/SKILL.md` under
  `src/coga/resources/templates/coga/bootstrap/skills/`, “Inbound references”.
  Its procedure searches both full path and leaf, excludes tickets/log and
  restricted trees, classifies matches, and pins real references in a PR.
- Cited rather than attached: read `coga-dev/testing` at
  `docs/contexts/coga-dev/testing/SKILL.md`, “Verification tiers and receipts”.

'''
s=s[:a]+spec+s[b:]

Inspected clean `main` at `b23d6db94a64b5153a9448091e110d0c6f259ef7`;
no task feature branch or PR is recorded, so no branch PR merge check applies.
The configured origin is a local bare trial remote; fetched and fast-forward
check passed before design. No implementation code, branch, or PR created.

Proposal: advisory candidate warnings on stderr from shared deletion, never a

Literal false positives are an explicit tradeoff; excluded archives and failed

The design is for evaluator and owner review, not self-approved.

## Open Questions

None requiring unavailable input for this design step. Warning policy and
retire's lack of automatic repair are concrete proposals for the owner gate.''')

at a path that no longer exists on the control branch. Retro already searches
for and reviews those references, but ordinary `coga delete`, the `delete-task`
recipe, and deterministic retirement of done tickets bypass that procedure.

unattended deletion and existing exit/publication contracts; this is a warning,
not a proof that a link is broken or a refusal gate.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Before filesystem removal, `coga delete`, `coga run delete-task`, and
  done-ticket `coga retire` report candidate inbound references on stderr.
  Each diagnostic identifies the deleted task and referring repo-relative
  file and line, says deletion will continue, and advises inspecting live
  references and pinning them to a commit containing the ticket before
  deleting (or restoring the ticket and repairing afterward).
- [ ] Search tracked working-tree files with literal matching for both the
  resolved task's Git-root-relative removal path and its final slug component
  without `.md`. This catches control-branch URLs, full paths, and relative
  file/directory links, including nested task slugs. Resolve paths from config
  and `TaskRef`, never by assuming `coga/tasks` or the invocation directory.
- [ ] Exclude the configured tasks root (all transient tickets), configured
  global log file, and `docs/archive/**` before reading file contents. Scan
  from the actual Git root, including files outside a nested Coga workspace.
  Do not read untracked/ignored files or follow symlinks out of the tree.
  Duplicate pattern matches on one source line produce one diagnostic entry.
- [ ] Describe hits as *possible references*: longer slugs, fixture text, and
  existing commit permalinks can match and require human inspection. No
  Markdown parser or semantic link classifier is required. No claim that a
  quiet search proves deletion safe; untracked content, excluded trees, and
  other checkouts are outside this check.
- [ ] A successful scan with no matches is quiet. Disabled Git, missing Git,
  a non-Git workspace, or a failed scan produces one concise stderr warning
  that references were not checked, and deletion still proceeds. A grep exit
  of 1 means no matches; other failures must not masquerade as a clean scan.
  Expected scan failures never escape as tracebacks or `DeleteTaskError`.
- [ ] Existing stdout deletion reports, success/error exit codes, task-shape
  safety, checkout lock, publication boundaries, and retire checkout refusal
  stay intact. No confirmation, force flag, Slack notification, link edit,
  new task, or Retro agent is added for done-ticket retirement.
- [ ] Recurring same-path replacement does not warn about links to the path it
  immediately recreates. Ordinary removal, including recurring promotion,
  uses the shared warning behavior. Cover this exception explicitly rather
  than relying on a caller discarding the deletion report.
- [ ] Regression tests cover all three command routes, both ticket shapes,
  nested/custom workspace paths, working-tree edits to tracked references,
  exclusions, false positives, no matches, scan errors/unavailable Git, and
  the recurring replacement exception. Verify warning emission occurs while
